pairs.subject: crash-forensics-attribution
pairs.evidence: src/components/modules/evaluator/CrashAnalyzerView/CrashDetailPanel.tsx:68 When the module gate declines, the UI shows only the words 'module not determined'. It does not say which gate failed (no-evidence vs ambiguous), the top two candidates with their scores, or the contributing frames, so the honest unknown carries none of the information the standard requires an unknown to carry.

techniques.evidence: src/components/modules/evaluator/CrashAnalyzerView/CrashDetailPanel.tsx:68 Unknown is labelled, but the reason, the top two with scores and the evidence frames are absent. An attributed module is likewise shown with no score, margin or basis.

src/components/modules/evaluator/CrashAnalyzerView/PlainCrashSummary.tsx:63 Technical mode labels a transferred diagnosis correctly (AiDiagnosisCard.tsx:116 'computed confidence … signature similarity'), and NoDiagnosisNotice shows the near miss against the floor. But Plain mode never checks diagnosis.match, so a signature-matched diagnosis is presented as 'analysis of this crash'. Matched evidence is shown as if it were freshly derived.

src/components/modules/evaluator/CrashAnalyzerView/PlainCrashSummary.tsx:31 The fault-class 'what happened / what to do' layer is read from the single glossary module and offered as a Plain/Technical mode (PlainModeToggle). The raw log and callstack stay available behind a disclosure.

src/components/modules/evaluator/CrashAnalyzerView/AiDiagnosisCard.tsx:146 The fix prompt is offered as 'one-click' and rendered verbatim. The prompts it shows (sample-crashes.ts:293) prescribe defensive null-check guards and 'Verify the build compiles', i.e. structural-only verification, and the card adds no behavioural verification or prohibitions.
